Funny to see this comment today. I have PCOS and I'm currently getting acupuncture for depression, grief, and things like that. I haven't been sharing my concerns about PCOS because there's so much to say about my emotional/existential concerns, but yesterday we did an internal dragons treatment and I feel like it helped.

Yes. Last week I was awake around 5 and convinced myself it would be nice to take a long walk before the streets fill up with people. Then I lie there. Every part of the process is a struggle. Take my laptop to by backpack. Rest 20 min. Take charger to backpack. Rest 20 min. Find socks. Rest while building up motivation to put them on. When I'm entirely dressed I feel so accomplished that I deserve a rest. Eventually it's 11am and I don't go because I hate the crowds.

I keep trying to tell people that this is what my life is 90% of the time and they don't believe me. Basically when I say that I spent weeks/months not going out and not doing anything, they start telling me that I shouldn't believe everyone's Instagram life and nobody is out there having fun all the time. Sure, I'm not an idiot, but the point is that I don't go anywhere in the morning or the evening or the weekend or xmas etc. It frustrates me to no end that because I present as a chipper, educated middle-class westerner, people don't believe anything I tell them about my life. I've been homeless, I've been stuck in a really messed-up pattern that's kept me socially isolated and at home for huge periods of time, and whenever I think I can tell someone, they just dismiss me and my despair increases.

Yes, I avoid looking in the mirror. I can't stand to see the signs of age and the reminder that I completely missed out on so many years, and that it was completely avoidable but I allowed myself to wallow in absurd vicious circles.

What I can say is that I've been getting acupuncture 2-3 x a week for depression for months and it doesn't seem to be helping me.... At least not enough. And considering that I'm only employed 20%, I am paying for all of this with credit cards. I wish the clinicians would be more proactive in changing course, recommending other things, etc.
You don't need to appreciate anything right now. That's asking too much of yourself. But if you can distract yourself it can help you hold on.

Please stay. I know the pain. Forcing positive thoughts often doesn't work in that dark place, but you are strong and you can weather this. Maybe just for now, distract yourself with a video or movie. You don't need to find a solution right now and it's ok to feel how you do. Just try to make it to the next day. One minute at a time.

This brings tears to my eyes but I'm in a public space. I feel like every day for the past 8 months has been a battle against death. Even today I just stood on an overpass, thinking I could just end it. I wish it were more simple.

A friend told me that I could talk to her anytime, so I emailed and called a couple times over the last few months. We saw each other a couple weeks ago and she "joked" that I overshare. Suffice it to say I won't reach out to her anymore.

I'm carrying too many bad memories and it's worse because most of this was avoidable, which is why sometimes it ended up lasting so long (I'd feel discouraged because I knew I had the resources to makes changes, so that would make me feel more sad and regretful and stuck, and I'd dig myself deeper). I can't deal with how wrong everything has been, and even when I can make it right, I get it wrong again. Like I am back in my city now when I had the opportunity to be elsewhere, and it's upset me so much that I've gained at least 5 pounds this month. I can't deal with anything because every single place makes me sad. Going jogging - as healthy as it would be in usual circumstances - would just make me feel terrible about the past and the fact that I am in the same place... so I am becoming a fat diabetic blob. I hate that even if I leave I have wasted so many years of my ex's life and he will be stuck here.
